```lean
rfl.{u} {α : Sort u} {a : α} : a = a
```
***
`rfl : a = a` is the unique constructor of the equality type. This is the
same as `Eq.refl` except that it takes `a` implicitly instead of explicitly.

This is a more powerful theorem than it may appear at first, because although
the statement of the theorem is `a = a`, Lean will allow anything that is
definitionally equal to that type. So, for instance, `2 + 2 = 4` is proven in
Lean by `rfl`, because both sides are the same up to definitional equality.

```lean
Fintype.card_coe.{u_1} {α : Type u_1} (s : Finset α) [Fintype { x // x ∈ s }] : Fintype.card { x // x ∈ s } = s.card
```

*import Mathlib.Data.Fintype.Card*

```lean
Polynomial.derivative_map.{u, v} {R : Type u} {S : Type v} [Semiring R] [Semiring S] (p : R[X]) (f : R →+* S) :
  derivative (map f p) = map f (derivative p)
```
***
*import Mathlib.Algebra.Polynomial.Derivative*

```lean
Polynomial.card_roots_toFinset_le_derivative (p : ℝ[X]) : p.roots.toFinset.card ≤ (derivative p).roots.toFinset.card + 1
```
***
The number of roots of a real polynomial is at most the number of roots of its derivative plus
one.

```lean
Polynomial.card_rootSet_le_derivative.{u_1} {F : Type u_1} [CommRing F] [Algebra F ℝ] (p : F[X]) :
```
